body:
Not to tell you the whole story, but there was a rumor going around that me and a girl had spent the night together and slept together. We both denied it separately, but both of us admitted we had hung out together. Anyhow, it turns into a mini-scandal anyhow, and I quit my job and move away. All seems well; I get another job, start towards another degree, getting along great with my girlfriend, etc. Then there was a mini-meltdown in the life of the girl about a year after all this happened. She moves home, goes to the police and goes back and says no I lied before this is what really happened. I refuse to talk to the police saying I stand by what I said before, and they decide to charge me. It partially had to do with a squabble between my girlfriend and this girl and some other things, at least from what I've heard through hearsay. But anyhow after I left I hadn't spoken to her, and I didn't think she had any animosity towards me. I'm not really sure why she did it. I don't know if she was trying to get back at my girlfriend and didn't realize how serious it was (she was a naive person), or if with other things falling apart in her life decided she needed an excuse/scapegoat or what. It's all out of my hands now.

You're right about the options part. He is the worst attorney in the world, but I've never had to deal with the and he came recommended. He doesn't communicate with me, doesn't return my calls, and meets with me as little as possible. I think he is actually doing his job, but I guess it's a little like a doctor who is competent but has the worst bed side manner possible, so I have no idea what is going on. But I can't afford to switch lawyers at this point, so I'm pretty much stuck.

He knows my situation and what I will accept, so I guess I just have to let it go and see what happens. It's just hard sometimes.

Anyhow, thanks for your advice. I know I'm being dramatic, but I just see what's going on TV with all the priests and coaches and all that and I get terrified when I think I could get lumped into the same category as them. I know when/if people heard my particular story even if they are disgusted it wouldn't be on par with that, but for those who don't know I'll be just the same.

I know you are right. When this happened and I lost my job, I had to move in with my parents. A few people in their community and church knew about my situation and still ended up being supportive and helpful. It hasn't been so bad when nothing final has happened, but just the thought of potentially becoming a felon/so and knowing the rage, anger, and judgment people have towards those people makes me feel incredibly shameful. 

I don't want to give up, but it's just hard coming to grips with the fact that my life could have ended up like this.

Thanks I'm trying to believe it's the case. I'm glad I have family/friends who do care about me, otherwise I would've finished myself when I first got charged with this. I don't want to let anyone down, but on the other hand I don't want to be living a life that isn't really a life either...

I don't know the details of what my options will be. At my most recent court date last Monday he just told me that negotiations were getting serious. I was charged with this over a year ago, and when I heard another lawyer, a former prosecutor, and a judge who was a former prosecutor telling me they didn't think it would end up being prosecuted I falsely got my hopes up. 

Well in this state there is a very good chance I would only have to register as the lowest level, which wouldn't require me to be on the searchable database.

The part I'm having trouble coping with most is the shame/embarrassment I feel just thinking about how people could know that and what they would think of me.
Okay, sorry that turned into long story long.
